title: Zest AI Restaurant Concierge Launches With Text Booking
summary: Zest's new AI agent finds restaurants and books reservations via text message. Integrates credit card data for personalized recommendations and group dining.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- Zest officially launched its AI restaurant concierge agent on October 30, 2026, enabling users to discover dining spots and book tables via text.
- The agent analyzes credit card transaction history through Plaid to deliver personalized recommendations without lengthy onboarding conversations.
- Group chat integration allows the AI to blend multiple users' preferences, facilitate voting, and book reservations for entire parties in-thread.


Zest, the restaurant discovery startup founded in November 2024, officially launched its AI-powered restaurant concierge agent on October 30, 2026. The new feature shifts restaurant recommendations and table bookings into text messages, marking a strategic pivot from standalone mobile apps to conversational AI interfaces. Users can now text (212) 470-6067 to access personalized dining suggestions and immediate reservation capabilities through OpenTable, Resy, and SevenRooms integrations.


The launch reflects founder and CEO Mario Gomez-Hall's vision that conversational agents are replacing traditional app experiences. "The agent is the product now," Gomez-Hall explained, emphasizing how Zest's credit card integration provides immediate personalization without weeks of training conversations.


## How Zest's AI Restaurant Agent Works


Zest's concierge agent analyzes users' actual dining history by linking to credit card transactions through Plaid, the financial services platform used by banks and fintech apps. The system focuses exclusively on food and drink purchases to build personalized taste profiles. When users text the concierge, the AI draws from this transaction history to recommend restaurants that match their proven preferences, whether searching in their home city or traveling to new destinations.


Users can specify search criteria including cuisine type, dietary restrictions, neighborhood, occasion, or specific cravings. The agent answers questions about restaurant details like crowd levels, Wi-Fi availability, and menu options. If a suggestion looks promising, users can request the menu directly in the text thread before deciding to book a table.


## Group Chat Integration and Voting Features


One distinctive capability sets Zest apart from solo recommendation engines: the AI can join group text conversations to coordinate dining plans for multiple people. When added to a group chat, the concierge blends everyone's taste profiles to identify restaurants that will satisfy the entire party. An in-thread voting feature helps groups resolve indecision without leaving the conversation.


Once the group reaches consensus, Zest books the table for everyone through connected reservation platforms. This eliminates the typical back-and-forth of coordinating group dining plans across multiple apps and conversation threads.


## Release Date and Initial Testing


Officially launched on October 30, 2026, the restaurant concierge completed a month-long testing phase that began in September 2026. Zest delayed the public launch until it could integrate full booking capabilities alongside its recommendation engine. Early testing demonstrated the AI's ability to match suggestions to user preferences while considering time constraints, party size, location, and availability windows.


The company received $1.8 million in pre-seed funding from Alexis Ohanian's 776 and Steve Jang's Kindred Ventures to support development of both the original app and this new agent interface.


## Revenue Model and Future Expansion Plans


Zest plans to generate revenue through booking commissions when users reserve tables via OpenTable or Resy, with food ordering capabilities coming in future updates. "Booking and ordering are the first revenue lines," Gomez-Hall stated, noting that Zest's transaction-based learning model provides faster personalization than general AI assistants.


The startup is already considering expansion beyond restaurants into broader business recommendations, shopping suggestions, and other discovery categories. By moving to a text-based interface, Zest aims to scale beyond its initial user base of several thousand people who adopted the original credit card-linked app.


## What This Means for Restaurant Discovery


Zest's launch signals a broader industry shift toward conversational AI agents that replace specialized mobile apps. While restaurant booking apps have existed for years, the convenience of text-based interaction combined with credit card-informed personalization offers a more seamless experience. For users tired of juggling multiple apps to research, discuss, and book dining plans, Zest's integrated approach consolidates the entire process into a familiar messaging interface. As AI agents continue to absorb functions previously handled by standalone apps, text-based concierge services may become the preferred interface for time-sensitive, decision-heavy tasks like coordinating group meals.
